name: Can a pool be removed without damaging the rest of the yard?

mainEntity.name: How do contractors protect landscaping, patios, fences, and nearby structures during pool demolition?
mainEntity.text: How do contractors protect landscaping, patios, fences, and nearby structures during pool demolition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pool removal can be done cleanly, but it requires more than breaking up the shell. Contractors should map the access route, protect existing hardscape, cover nearby structures, mark irrigation and lighting lines, and control where debris is staged. This is especially important in compact Los Angeles lots where pools sit close to fences, patios, or the house. If a crew drives heavy equipment across soft landscaping or uses the wrong loading plan, repairs can quickly become expensive. Before hiring, ask whether the estimate includes protection of trees, pavers, coping, lighting, sprinklers, and retaining walls. It also helps to ask how soil, dust, and broken concrete will be contained. A well-managed removal should leave the surrounding yard intact except for the pool footprint and any necessary access path. The fewer surprises in the plan, the less chance of collateral damage.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but only if the contractor plans for protection before demolition starts. Crews should protect hardscape, isolate equipment routes, and control dust and debris. Without that planning, pool removal can damage plants, paving, irrigation lines, and adjacent walls.
